name: Albert Einstein
info: Albert Einstein (1879–1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist, later a Swiss and American citizen, who developed the theory of relativity, made important contributions to quantum theory and received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

facts.born: 14 March 1879 in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire; son of the secular Ashkenazi Jews Hermann Einstein, a salesman and engineer, and Pauline Koch
facts.died: 18 April 1955 at Princeton Hospital, aged 76, after the rupture of an abdominal aortic aneurysm on 17 April; he refused surgery
facts.role: Theoretical physicist; patent examiner in Bern (from 1902); professor at Zurich, Prague and the ETH Zurich (1909–1914); member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences and professor at the Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1914); first director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics (from 1917); resident scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton (1933–1955)
facts.known: the special theory of relativity (1905) and the equivalence of mass and energy; the general theory of relativity (1915); the explanation of Brownian motion; the light quantum and the photoelectric effect; Bose–Einstein statistics; his objections to quantum mechanics and the EPR paper; the letter to Roosevelt of 1939

t: Working as a patent examiner in Bern, Einstein published four papers in 1905 on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and the equivalence of mass and energy, and in 1915 proposed the general theory of relativity.

Eddington's observations of a solar eclipse on 29 May 1919 were consistent with his calculations, and newspapers around the world reported them, which made Einstein, in one writer's phrase, perhaps the world's first celebrity scientist.

Driven out of Germany by the Nazis in 1933, he settled at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he signed the 1939 letter to President Roosevelt on nuclear weapons and spent his last decades disputing quantum mechanics and seeking a unified field theory.
dyk: Einstein's doctoral dissertation of 1905, on molecular dimensions, was 24 pages long and dedicated to his friend Marcel Grossmann; he was formally awarded his PhD on 15 January 1906.
ev: Born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, on 14 March
Renounces his Württemberg citizenship on 28 January and enrols at the federal polytechnic school in Zurich
Marries Mileva Marić in January; the Swiss Patent Office makes his position as assistant examiner permanent
Publishes four papers on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and the equivalence of mass and energy
Proposes the general theory of relativity, extending his mechanics to include gravitation
Eddington's observations of the solar eclipse of 29 May give results consistent with his calculations, and the press reports them worldwide
Surrenders his passport in Antwerp after the Nazis take power, and in October takes up a post at the Institute for Advanced Study
Dies at Princeton Hospital on 18 April, aged 76

sections.early:
Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg in the German Empire, on 14 March 1879. His parents, secular Ashkenazi Jews, were Hermann Einstein, a salesman and engineer, and Pauline Koch. In 1880 the family moved to Munich, where his father and his uncle Jakob founded a company that made electrical equipment based on direct current. His parents worried that he had a learning disability because he was very slow to learn to talk. When he was five and sick in bed, his father brought him a compass, which sparked a lifelong fascination with electromagnetism. He attended a Catholic elementary school from the age of five and at eight moved to the Luitpold Gymnasium.

He began teaching himself algebra, calculus and Euclidean geometry at twelve, and at thirteen a family tutor, Max Talmud, introduced him to Kant's Critique of Pure Reason. In 1894 his father's firm lost a bid to light Munich because it lacked the capital to change from direct to alternating current, and the family moved to Italy, first to Milan and then to Pavia. Einstein, then fifteen, stayed behind to finish school. He later wrote that the Gymnasium's strict rote learning was harmful to creativity, and at the end of December 1894 a doctor's letter persuaded its authorities to release him. In 1895 he failed the general part of the entrance examination for the polytechnic school in Zurich but did well in physics and mathematics, and he completed his schooling at the cantonal school in Aarau, graduating in 1896.
sections.rise:
On 28 January 1896, six weeks before he turned seventeen, Einstein renounced his Württemberg citizenship, which avoided conscription into military service. He then enrolled in the four-year mathematics and physics teaching diploma programme at the Zurich polytechnic school. His friend Marcel Grossmann helped him get by despite his loose study habits, and among his fellow students was Mileva Marić, with whom he spent many hours discussing physics. They became lovers; a daughter, Lieserl, was born in early 1902, and what happened to her is uncertain. They married in January 1903.

Einstein graduated in 1900 and acquired Swiss citizenship in February 1901. Swiss schools offered him no teaching post despite almost two years of applications, and with the help of Grossmann's father he secured a post at the Swiss Patent Office in Bern as an assistant examiner, level III; it was made permanent in 1903. In 1902 he and his friends Conrad Habicht and Maurice Solovine formed a discussion group, the Olympia Academy, which read Henri Poincaré, Ernst Mach and David Hume. His doctoral dissertation was completed on 30 April 1905.

The academic path then opened. In 1908 he became a junior teacher at the University of Bern, in 1909 an associate professor at Zurich, in 1911 a full professor in Prague, and in July 1912 a professor of theoretical physics at the ETH Zurich. In 1913 Max Planck and Walther Nernst offered him membership of the Prussian Academy of Sciences, the directorship of a planned physics institute and a Berlin chair with no teaching duties, and he moved there in April 1914.
sections.deeds:
In 1905, sometimes described as his annus mirabilis, Einstein published four papers in the Annalen der Physik. They outlined a theory of the photoelectric effect, explained Brownian motion, introduced the special theory of relativity and showed that mass and energy are equivalent. In the paper on moving bodies, received on 30 June, he reconciled conflicts between Maxwell's equations and Newtonian mechanics by changing the laws of mechanics, and argued that the luminiferous aether was superfluous. The relativity work remained controversial for many years but was accepted by leading physicists, starting with Max Planck.

From 1907 he worked towards a new theory of gravitation, beginning with the equivalence principle. After a false start with the Entwurf theory of 1913, which he abandoned in November 1915, he completed the general theory of relativity that year, using Riemannian geometry, and applied it to the precession of Mercury's perihelion. Observations by Sir Arthur Eddington during the total eclipse of 29 May 1919 yielded results consistent with his calculations, and on 7 November 1919 The Times printed the headline "Revolution in Science – New Theory of the Universe – Newtonian Ideas Overthrown".

In 1917 he applied general relativity to the universe as a whole, introducing the cosmological constant, and wrote a paper proposing stimulated emission. In 1924 he translated and supported a paper by Satyendra Nath Bose, which led to Bose–Einstein statistics. He became the first director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics in 1917 and received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded in 1922, for the law of the photoelectric effect.
sections.opponents:
His light quanta were nearly universally rejected by physicists, including Max Planck and Niels Bohr, and the Nobel citation of 1922 did not assent to his notion of the particulate nature of light. After 1925 he grew displeased with quantum mechanics as it had evolved, objecting that God "is not playing at dice", and he maintained to the end of his life that the theory was incomplete. His public disputes with Bohr are remembered for their importance to the philosophy of science. In 1935 he published with Boris Podolsky and Nathan Rosen the paper known as the EPR paradox. In 1964 John Stewart Bell showed that hidden variables would have to be nonlocal, and said the paradox "is resolved in the way which Einstein would have liked least". His search for a unified field theory did not succeed, and he became isolated from mainstream physics.

His private life drew criticism too. In 1912 he began a relationship with Elsa Löwenthal; when Marić learned of it in 1914 she returned to Zurich with their sons, Hans Albert and Eduard, and the couple were divorced on 14 February 1919. He married Löwenthal in 1919. Eduard was diagnosed with schizophrenia and lived the rest of his life in his mother's care or in an asylum. Historians of physics are divided on how far Marić contributed to the 1905 papers.

His travel diary of 1922 recorded views of Chinese people, and of Indian people, that were uncomplimentary; of the Chinese he wrote that "even the children are spiritless and look obtuse". Some argue that signing the 1939 letter to Roosevelt went against his pacifist principles. In Germany the Nazis targeted his works in the book burnings of 1933, and one magazine listed him as an enemy of the regime, "not yet hanged", with a bounty on his head.
sections.last:
In February 1933, while visiting the United States, Einstein knew he could not return to Germany after Adolf Hitler came to power. The Gestapo repeatedly raided his Berlin apartment, and the Nazis raided his cottage, confiscated his sailboat and later converted the cottage into a Hitler Youth camp. On landing in Antwerp on 28 March he surrendered his passport at the German consulate; the Nazi government revoked his citizenship on 24 March 1934. He stayed in Belgium and then in England, where he asked Winston Churchill and others to help bring Jewish scientists out of Germany. His letter to Turkey's prime minister İsmet İnönü in September 1933 led to invitations to over 1,000 people. In October he took up a position at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, which he held until his death. Elsa died in December 1936, and he became an American citizen in 1940.

In July 1939 Leó Szilárd and Eugene Wigner visited him to explain the possibility of atomic bombs, and he signed a letter with Szilárd to President Roosevelt recommending that the United States begin its own nuclear weapons research. In 1954 he told Linus Pauling that signing it was "one great mistake in my life", though there was some justification. In 1955 he and ten others signed a manifesto on the danger of nuclear weapons.

In 1952, after Chaim Weizmann died, David Ben-Gurion offered him the presidency of Israel, which he declined. On 17 April 1955 an abdominal aortic aneurysm ruptured; he refused surgery, saying "It is tasteless to prolong life artificially", and died early the next morning at the age of 76. A pathologist removed his brain without the family's permission. His ashes were scattered at an undisclosed location.
sections.legacy:
Einstein left his papers and literary estate to the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, which he had helped to establish. The release of more than 30,000 unique documents was announced in 2014. In his final four years he was also involved in founding the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York City, and the element einsteinium was named in his honour in 1955.

Several of his predictions were confirmed long after he made them. Gravitational waves, predicted in 1916, were first observed directly by researchers at LIGO, who published their result on 11 February 2016, and a Bose–Einstein condensate was first produced experimentally in 1995. His 1917 paper on stimulated emission describes the process that makes the laser and maser possible. The EPR paper, which Einstein himself found overly complicated, became among the most influential papers published in Physical Review and is considered a centrepiece of the development of quantum information theory. Most researchers now believe his approach to unifying physics was mistaken, but his goal of a theory of everything is one to which his successors still aspire.

The Times and other newspapers made him an intellectual icon after 1919, and his name became synonymous with genius in popular culture. The physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, speaking at UNESCO in 1965, remembered in him "a wonderful purity at once childlike and profoundly stubborn". Einstein described himself as a "deeply religious nonbeliever" and said he had sympathy for the impersonal God of Spinoza.

summary: Albert Einstein (1879–1955), born in Ulm and later a Swiss and American citizen, published four papers in 1905 while a patent examiner and proposed the general theory of relativity in 1915. Forced out of Germany in 1933, he settled at Princeton, where he disputed quantum mechanics.
references: Ronald W. Clark, Einstein: The Life and Times (Avon Books, 1971)
Walter Isaacson, Einstein: His Life and Universe (Simon & Schuster, 2007)
Jürgen Neffe, Einstein: A Biography (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2007)
Abraham Pais, Subtle is the Lord: The Science and the Life of Albert Einstein (Oxford University Press, 1982)
notes: Dates: start 1879 and end 1955 as the article gives them; no hedging.

Role fact: 'patent examiner (from 1902)' follows the article's section heading 'Assistant at the Swiss Patent Office (1902–1909)'; the text itself gives only the permanent post of 1903. The Prague post is dated 1911 (the role fact says 1909–1914 for Zurich, Prague and ETH, which loosely covers 1909 to 1914 and the Berlin move in April 1914).

Citizenship: the article says he renounced Württemberg citizenship on 28 January 1896; the lead says he acquired Swiss citizenship 'a year later' than 1900, while the text gives February 1901 (used). In 1933 the article says he surrendered his passport on 28 March and that the Nazi government revoked citizenship on 24 March 1934; the article's own date of the Enabling Act (23 March) precedes his landing, consistent. In 1914 he became a Prussian and German citizen again (not stated in the text).
Marriage: the article says Einstein was divorced from Marić on 14 February 1919 and married Löwenthal in 1919; the second marriage's month is not given.
Dissertation: lead says PhD submitted in 1905; text says completed 30 April 1905, approved three months later, PhD formally awarded 15 January 1906.

Nobel: the article says the 1921 prize was carried forward and awarded in 1922; the sections use 'awarded in 1922'. The article is not explicit that the Nobel prize was for 1921 in the first paragraph of the Awards section beyond the carried-forward remark.

Disputed or hedged points left out: Mileva Marić's contribution is given as scholars divided; Lieserl's fate uncertain; the 'biggest blunder' remark about the cosmological constant (Livio doubts it) and the steady-state manuscript of 1931 were left out for space.

Left out: music and violin, vegetarianism, the Zionist positions in detail (he opposed an independent Jewish state, then by 1947 supported partition), his political views on socialism, the FBI dossier, civil rights work with the NAACP and Du Bois, the Einstein refrigerator, the Einstein–de Haas experiment, polls and rankings (Time's Person of the Century, 1999 physicists' survey), the Albert Einstein Memorial, and the popular-culture section.
Place of death: the article says Princeton Hospital; cremated in Trenton, New Jersey.
Not in the article: the exact date he left Munich, details of the Marangoni family, anything on Einstein's views on Russia except Lenin remark (left out).
References: left empty for the editor.
